title: Variable-span bucketizer with prefill trim and kernel-aware routing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Long padding waste during prefill and decode increases token cost and throughput variability for mixed-length workloads. Goal: implement a variable-span bucketizer that dynamically groups requests by effective token span (prefill + expected decode) and performs selective prefix trimming at pack time. Combine this with a lightweight kernel-scoring heuristic that routes buckets to the optimal kernel variant (e.g., fused-attention, quantized MatMul, or slow-path reference) to reduce tail latency and unit cost. Success criteria: 15-30% average token-cost reduction for our benchmark suite, 5-15% p90 latency improvement for mixed workloads, and no regressions on accuracy or K-anon safety checks.
technical_design: Overview: Introduce a new 'span' metric computed per request: span = max(prefill_len_trimmed, estimate_decode_len). The bucketizer maintains soft buckets with variable boundaries (not fixed powers-of-two) optimized for observed span histogram using an online K-means-like updater.

Prefill trim policy: Apply conservative prefix-trimming heuristic only to prefill tokens that match a configurable whitelist pattern (e.g., repeated prompts, system templates) and when KV-cache reuse probability is low. Trim via logical offset (no model alteration) so outputs are reconstructable on the client by re-expanding the prefix metadata.

Kernel-aware routing: Each bucket computes a kernel score vector (latency_est, throughput_est, memory_est) using precomputed kernel profiles for (model, seq_len, hardware) triples. A simple cost function chooses the kernel variant that minimizes expected cost subject to latency SLOs. The runtime will fallback to alternative kernels if a kernel runs out of memory or reports high error rates.

Scheduler integration: Integrate with prefill/decode scheduler so that prefill packing and decode coalescing are aware of eventual decode expectations. Implement backpressure tokens that mark high-latency buckets for opportunistic packing with compatible requests.

State and metrics: Expose per-bucket metrics (requests, avg_span, fill_rate, kernel_selected, prefix_trimmed_pct) and add alerts when trimmed-prefix reconstruct rate < 99.9% or kernel fallback rate > 0.5%.

Safety and correctness: Reconstructability test harness and unit tests ensure trimmed prefixes do not change final logits for identical requests when re-expanded. Also ensure audit logs record all trimmed content for compliance customers.
Migration strategy: Start as opt-in via runtime flag + per-customer enablement. Gradually increase bucket counts and aggressiveness after observing stable metrics in canary region.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark suite (mixed lengths, 0-2048 tokens) shows >=15% average token cost reduction on nightly run compared to baseline packing
p90 decode latency improves by at least 5% on mixed workloads without violating existing SLOs for P99
No accuracy regressions on evaluation prompts (per-eval-suite diff < 0.1%)
End-to-end reconstructability test passes for 100k synthetic cases
Operational metrics (kernel fallback rate, trimmed-prefix reconstruct rate) are visible in the Console and thresholds configured
experiments: Exp A: conservative trim (only repeated-system prefixes) + 8 buckets: baseline cost -10%, p90 -4%
Exp B: moderate trim (templates + repeated tokens) + 16 buckets + kernel-aware routing: baseline cost -22%, p90 -9%
Exp C: aggressive trim (allow short user prefixes) + dynamic bucket merging: baseline cost -31% but increased fallback rate to 1.2% -> not acceptable
Kernel profiles collected on p4d and a100 clusters for seq_len = {64,128,256,512,1024,2048} to seed the score model
benchmark_results: Nightly run 2026-03-08 (canary region): mixed-workload throughput +18%, token-cost -20% (Exp B), p90 latency -8%
Canary regression check: no eval-suite diffs >0.05% across 12k eval prompts
Memory headroom: selected kernels reduced average GPU memory per-request by ~12% enabling 1.1x higher co-resident concurrency
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal testing on canary cluster with opt-in flag (2 weeks). Collect metrics and kernel fallback events.
Phase 1: Customer alpha (select Dedicated customers) with telemetry and explicit consent (4 weeks). Provide rollback knob per-customer.
Phase 2: Gradual global rollout for hosted API (8 weeks) with auto-throttle if fallback or reconstruct metrics breach thresholds.
Phase 3: Promote to default and tune bucket counts + trim aggressiveness based on observed span histograms and cost targets
